name: chat-composer
title: Composer
description: The person's message: the chips a host may attach, each removable; the host's context chip, one summary of what every message carries (on the board, "3 answers · 2 selected": the selected cards and the answers since the last Send, and no other chips), which opens a preview of exactly that text; the text and Send; and one line under it with the keys, why Send waits, or why the composer is shut (the Architect composer). With a host that queues (ChatHost.queues) words go while the agent works or waits for an OK, and the line says they are queued. With the host's words for attaching (view.files, D-068) it takes files by drop, paste and the paperclip, and shows a chip per file saying whether it is uploading, ready, or refused and why; the host uploads.

files.core: composer-core.ts (composerView, sendIntent, chipKey, withoutChip, ComposerContext, ComposerFile, ComposerFileWords, FileState, filesReady, filesUploading, filesSaid, pastedFiles, PREVIEW_LABEL, COMPOSER_KEYS; no DOM)
files.template: composer-template.ts (composerTemplate, chipsTemplate, contextTemplate, previewTemplate, lineTemplate, attachTemplate, dropTemplate, saidTemplate, fileTemplate)
files.element: chat-composer.ts (defineChatComposer, ChatComposerElement; light DOM); composer-attach.ts (the drop, the paste and the paperclip)

states: the preview open by hover, held open by click, Enter or Space
holding: what is attached waits for the turn to end
with the paperclip: idle, hover, focus, pressed, disabled when shut
a file dragged over it (data-drop): the box says what a drop does; only files, not text or a card
a file uploading: its mark turns, it says so on the chip, and the line says Send waits
a file refused: a row of its own with the reason in full; never sent
a file's remove button: idle, hover, focus, pressed

attributes.data-shut: the host's blocked reason applies: the text can't be typed in
attributes.data-drop: a file is being dragged over the composer

methods.show(view): Send allowed, the line, the placeholder, shut or not (from composerView)
methods.setContext(context): the host's context { label, text } beside the chips, or null: one chip, its summary, opening a preview of text exactly as it goes; not removable, it goes with every message the host sends
methods.setFiles(files): where each attached file stands: { id, name, state: uploading | ready | refused, reason }; the host's to say
methods.clear(): empties the words, the chips and the files once the message went through
methods.text, chips, attached, focusText(): the words typed, the chips, whether a chip, the context or a ready file is attached, focus into the text

events: chat-send (bubbles): detail { text, chips }; Enter or Send, with words while the conditions allow; with a host that holds what is attached (ChatHost.holds), also with no words and while the agent works when something is attached. The words stay until clear()
chat-chip-remove (bubbles): detail { chip }; the chip is taken off and focus goes back to the text
chat-files (bubbles): detail { files, pasted }; files dropped, pasted or picked, as File objects: the host uploads them
chat-file-remove (bubbles): detail { id }; a file's chip is taken off and focus goes back to the text
whenNotToUse: A note on a card (the note bubble).
accessibility: The text is labelled 'Message to the agent'. Enter sends, Shift+Enter breaks the line. Each chip's remove button is named 'Remove Card 12: <title>' or 'Remove Note: <text>', 24px square. The context chip is a button named by its summary, with aria-expanded; open, it controls the preview, a focusable region named 'What the agent receives' (a long one scrolls by keyboard). Hover opens it and keeps it while the pointer is on the chip or the preview; click, Enter or Space hold it open or close it; Esc closes it, focus on the chip, and goes no further (the board's Esc does not run). The paperclip is a button (Enter or Space opens the file picker), so dragging is never the only way (WCAG 2.5.7); named and tipped by the host's words. A status line (role=status) announces each file as it arrives, each change of state with its reason, and each removal; a state is in words as well as its mark, never by colour alone. A file's remove button is named by the file, 24px square, keeps focus when the row is drawn again, and sends focus to the text when pressed. Motion stops under prefers-reduced-motion. A name's direction comes from the name (dir=auto).
